preheader: Chip stocks drop nearly 11%, Zipline raises $1.5B, and 7-foot-9 Olivier Rioux dominates in his UCI debut.

lead.headline: Semiconductor stocks slide nearly 11% in steep market pullback
lead.body: The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plunged nearly 11 percent on Thursday, tracking toward its worst single-day drop since March 2020. Heavyweights including Nvidia, Broadcom, and AMD fell sharply as investors reconsidered heavy artificial intelligence infrastructure spending and political opposition to rapid data center expansion.
lead.why: When you evaluate tech companies or pitch investment ideas, watch how quickly shifts in capital spending expectations can drag down an entire supply chain.

stories.headline: Legal AI unicorn Harvey explores an initial public offering
stories.body: Harvey, an artificial intelligence startup focused on legal workflows, has held preliminary discussions with law firm Latham & Watkins about going public. The startup was recently valued at $15.5 billion.
stories.why: Tracking high-valuation AI startups as they approach the public markets will help you analyze how software multiples hold up outside the venture capital bubble.

stories.headline: Food delivery startup Wonder files confidentially for an IPO
stories.body: Wonder has submitted confidential paperwork for an initial public offering following several years of aggressive fundraising and acquisitions. The filing marks a key step toward listing shares on the public market.
stories.why: Understanding how food delivery models try to prove profitable unit economics gives you practical context for consumer tech case studies at Merage.

stories.headline: Anthropic adds personal finance tracking directly into Claude
stories.body: Anthropic launched a personal finance tool that lets Claude connect to your bank accounts on a read-only basis. The model can tally spending, flag duplicate or unusual charges, and categorize monthly expenses, though it cannot initiate transfers.
stories.why: For student builders, this highlights how major AI labs are moving from open-ended chatbots toward vertical software tools designed for personal budgeting and financial analysis.

stories.headline: Anthropic brings in outside researchers to audit safety before its public debut
stories.body: Anthropic invited researchers from the Berkeley nonprofit Model Evaluation and Threat Research to review its internal data and interview team members. The audit arrives as the company readies its Wall Street debut and addresses debate over advanced model safety.
stories.why: Third-party risk auditing and compliance will be massive practice areas for management consultants advising enterprise technology firms.

stories.headline: Bain Capital's Special Situations team deploys $1.2B in 2026
stories.body: Bain Capital's Special Situations group has deployed $1.2 billion this year and aims to maintain a $1 billion annual pace. Partner Sarit Chopra noted increasing corporate demand for hybrid capital as alternatives to traditional bank loans remain scarce.
stories.why: Special situations and structured finance desks provide a direct path into private markets, combining balance sheet restructuring with flexible debt investing.

stories.headline: Block cuts staff in its second round of layoffs this year
stories.body: Jack Dorsey's fintech company Block informed staff that it is eliminating positions, shifting responsibilities, and reorganizing reporting lines. The move marks the company's second workforce reduction in 2026.
stories.why: Tech firms continue to prioritize lean operations, so framing your internship projects around measurable cost savings and operational efficiency will stand out.

stories.headline: 7-foot-9 Olivier Rioux delivers a double-double in UC Irvine debut
stories.body: The tallest player in college basketball history made his Anteater debut on Tuesday night at the Bren Events Center. Center Olivier Rioux recorded 13 points and 12 rebounds in 18 minutes to help UC Irvine defeat Chapman 92-66.

stories.headline: Novak Djokovic exits Paris Masters, concluding his 2026 season
stories.body: Novak Djokovic lost in three sets to Australia's Rinky Hijikata in the second round of the Paris Masters. The defeat ends Djokovic's 2026 campaign, disqualifies him from the ATP Finals, and snaps a 21-year streak.

term.name: Market correction
term.definition: A market correction is a drop of 10 percent or more from a recent high in an individual stock or index. It is less severe than a bear market, which requires a 20 percent decline. On Thursday, tech indices moved into correction territory as investors quickly dialed back expectations for semiconductor and artificial intelligence infrastructure spending.

serve.headline: Zipline raised $1.5B at a $21.5B valuation to scale autonomous drone deliveries
serve.body: Autonomous drone startup Zipline secured $1.5 billion in new funding, nearly tripling its valuation in 10 months. The capital will support US expansion alongside an agreement with Walmart to add 300 drone delivery locations.
